top_jobs.job: When the bank looks thin ahead of a supplier deposit and payroll, help me see the lowest cash day in the next 13 weeks and what to move, so I never scramble for a panic loan
top_jobs.metric: lowest projected cash balance in the next 13 weeks against the cash floor, weekly

top_jobs.job: When revenue is up but the bank is not, help me see what each product, channel and sale really made after every cost, so I grow the parts that make money
top_jobs.metric: contribution margin per product and channel after marketing, monthly

top_jobs.job: When the agency asks for more ad budget, help me set the most I can spend and still make money, and see whether we are buying new customers or only rebuying old ones, so I say yes or no with a number
top_jobs.metric: total sales divided by total ad spend against the break-even line, weekly

top_jobs.job: When costs creep up one bill at a time, from apps nobody uses to payment fees to sales tax, help me find the leaks and what we owe, so profit stops leaking and no letter surprises me
top_jobs.metric: overhead against plan by line, monthly, and states near their sales tax limit

jobs.job: Build the 13 week cash forecast: bank balance today, payouts by day, bills, payroll, supplier deposits, ad plan and loan payments, and mark the lowest cash day against the floor

inputs.need: bank balance and 90 days of transactions
inputs.from: a read-only bank feed or the accounting tool

inputs.need: other payouts: PayPal, marketplaces, installment lenders
open bills, payroll and loan payments
purchase orders with deposit and balance dates
ad budget per week and the cash floor

steps: Start from today's bank balance
Add expected payouts by day, from the sales run rate and each processor's payout delay
Subtract bills, payroll, rent, supplier deposits and balances, loan payments and planned ad spend, by week
Mark the lowest day and the gap to the floor
Founder checks the big lines and adds anything missing
Each Monday compare last week's forecast with what happened and note the miss
jobs.output: a 13 week table with the lowest cash day, the gap to the floor, and last week's forecast error
jobs.next: feeds 21-03 (order test), 21-04 (which bills first), 21-05 (financing) and 19-02 (order size)

watch.metric: lowest projected cash balance in the next 13 weeks against the floor

jobs.job: Check every payout each day against what was expected from orders and processor terms, and list the late or short ones with the reason: reserve, hold, chargeback or bank holiday

inputs.need: Shopify Payments payouts, disputes and reserves
PayPal, Stripe, installment lender and marketplace payouts

steps: Compute the expected payout per source per day from orders, fees and payout delay
Match each to a bank deposit by amount and date
List late or short payouts with the reason given in the processor report
Draft the chase note for each, and a person sends it
jobs.output: a daily payout table with gaps and reasons

watch.metric: payouts late or short against expected, by source

jobs.job: Test a big purchase order against cash before signing: add its deposit and balance dates to a 26 week forecast, show the lowest point, and price 3 fixes: split shipment, longer terms, smaller first order
jobs.trigger: before any order over 20 percent of monthly revenue
steps: Add the order's cash out dates, and the sales it brings in, by week
Show the lowest cash point over 26 weeks
Price 3 fixes: 2 shipments, 30/70 terms, 70 percent of units first
Founder picks one, and the ask to the supplier is drafted
jobs.output: a cash test for the order with 3 options and the founder's pick

watch.metric: lowest cash in 26 weeks with the order, against the floor

jobs.job: When several bills fall in a short week, rank them by late fee, supplier importance and grace days, and set the pay order that keeps cash above the floor
jobs.trigger: weekly, when the forecast dips under the floor
steps: List bills due in the next 2 weeks with amount, due date, late fee and grace days
Mark the must-pay bills: payroll, tax, critical suppliers
Order the rest by cost of paying late
Show cash each day under the plan, and the founder approves
jobs.output: a pay now, pay later list with dates

watch.metric: bills paid late and late fees paid

jobs.job: Price every financing offer in plain terms: the true yearly cost of Shopify Capital, a revenue loan or a credit line, with the repayments dropped into the forecast to show the lowest cash with and without

inputs.need: offer terms: amount, fee, holdback share

steps: Turn the fee and holdback into a yearly cost, from how fast sales would repay it
Model repayments by day from the sales run rate
Show the lowest cash with and without the loan
Show what the money would buy (stock, ads) and the profit it should return
Founder decides, and the reason is logged
jobs.output: a 1 page note per offer: yearly cost, cash effect, profit case

watch.metric: true yearly cost of each offer, and lowest cash with repayments

jobs.job: Each month set aside estimated income tax, and show the owner the amount they can safely draw without breaking the cash plan

inputs.need: tax rate estimate and payment dates

steps: Estimate tax due on profit to date and the next payment date
Move the set-aside amount out of free cash in the forecast
Safe draw = lowest cash in 13 weeks, minus the floor, minus the tax set aside, minus a margin
Founder confirms the draw, and it goes into the forecast
jobs.output: a monthly tax set-aside and a safe draw number

watch.metric: tax set aside against estimated tax due

jobs.job: Build contribution margin by product and channel every month: sales after discounts and returns, minus landed cost, shipping, packing, payment and marketplace fees, and ad spend, and mark the products that lose money

inputs.need: shipping and packing cost per order
ad spend by campaign and landing page

steps: Compute each cost per order line
Assign ad spend to products by landing page and to channels by campaign
Compute contribution per product and channel from totals
Mark products with contribution under zero or under the floor
Founder reviews each loser: fix, reprice, or cut
jobs.output: a monthly margin table by product and channel, with a founder note on each loser

watch.metric: contribution margin per product and channel after marketing

jobs.job: Before a sale runs, compute the extra orders it needs to break even after product cost, shipping, fees and returns, and set that next to the lift the last 3 sales really got

inputs.need: orders from the last 3 sales and the weeks after

steps: Compute contribution per order at full price and at the sale price
Break-even lift = how many more orders the sale needs to make the same profit
Measure lift from the last 3 sales, after the dip in the weeks that followed
Write go, change the depth, or no, with the numbers
Founder decides
jobs.output: a 1 page promo check with break-even lift and past lift

watch.metric: profit per order at the sale price against break-even

jobs.job: Read each big sale 6 weeks after it ends: profit after returns, the dip in the weeks after, and the share of buyers who were new, next to a normal month
steps: Compute contribution for the sale weeks after returns and ad spend
Compare the 4 weeks after with a normal month to size the dip
Split buyers into new and returning
Write the verdict: made money or not, and what to change next time
Log it as a win or a fail in the ledger
jobs.output: a sale readout with profit, the dip after, new buyer share, and a win or fail note

watch.metric: contribution margin of the sale period after returns

jobs.job: Count shipping honestly: net shipping cost per order (carrier bill minus shipping charged) by order size, and test moving the free shipping line to where most orders clear it with profit
steps: Compute net shipping cost per order and as a share of revenue
Split by order value band
Model 2 new free shipping lines: orders lost, order value gained, shipping saved
Founder picks one to test for 4 weeks
jobs.output: a shipping cost table, and a free shipping line test

watch.metric: net shipping cost as a share of revenue

jobs.job: Each month, explain in 5 lines why profit and cash moved differently: stock bought, payouts in transit, loan principal, bills paid or owed, and tax

inputs.need: profit and loss for the month
bank balance at start and end

steps: Take profit for the month
Add and subtract: stock change, payouts not yet landed, loan principal, change in unpaid bills, tax paid
Check that the result equals the change in the bank, and name any gap left
Write 5 lines the founder can read in 1 minute
jobs.output: a monthly profit to cash bridge in 5 lines

watch.metric: gap between monthly profit and change in cash, with named causes

jobs.job: Set the ad spend line from real margin: compute the break-even and target ratio of total sales to total ad spend, check it weekly, and answer the agency's next budget ask with it

inputs.need: total ad spend on every platform

steps: Compute contribution margin before ads as a share of sales
Break-even ratio = 1 divided by that share; the target ratio leaves the profit goal
Compute the weekly ratio from totals and set it next to both lines
Split by new and returning customer sales, so repeat sales do not hide a weak first order
Write the budget answer: the most weekly spend that still clears the line
jobs.output: a weekly chart with break-even and target lines, and a 1 line budget answer

watch.metric: total store sales divided by total ad spend against break-even

jobs.job: Split profit into new and returning customers: first order contribution per new customer minus the cost to get them, and the months each cohort takes to pay back
steps: Cost per new customer = total ad spend divided by new customers, from totals
Compute first order contribution per new customer
Add up contribution by month per cohort until it passes the cost to get them
Mark cohorts that never pay back within 12 months
Set the most we can pay for a new customer, and log it on the finance shelf
jobs.output: a payback table by cohort, and a cap on cost per new customer

watch.metric: months for a new customer cohort to pay back its cost
watch.source: orders by cohort and ad spend

jobs.job: Find where the next $10,000 of marketing earns the most profit: read the last 12 weeks of spend steps per channel and the profit that followed, and say which channel to add to, or whether to keep the cash
jobs.trigger: monthly, or when extra budget appears
steps: For each channel, pair weeks where spend rose with the change in new customers and contribution
Estimate profit per extra dollar with a range, and mark weak reads
Compare with keeping the cash for stock or debt
Write 1 recommendation and a small test to confirm it
jobs.output: a table of profit per extra dollar per channel, and 1 recommendation

watch.metric: profit from added spend per channel

jobs.job: Forecast next quarter's sales in 2 parts, returning sales from past cohorts' repeat curves and new sales from planned spend and cost per new customer, and check last quarter's forecast against actual

inputs.from: Meta Ads, Google Ads and Shopify

steps: Project returning sales from each past cohort's repeat curve
Project new customers from planned spend divided by cost per new customer, with a range
Add peaks and launches from the calendar
Compare last quarter's forecast with actual and note the miss
Founder signs the number used for stock and hiring
jobs.output: a quarterly forecast split into new and returning, with last quarter's error

watch.metric: forecast against actual sales, new and returning

jobs.job: List every app and subscription from the store admin and the card statement with its monthly cost, last use and owner, and cancel the ones nobody used in 60 days

inputs.from: a bank feed, or the founder's export

inputs.need: last login or use per tool

steps: Pull every app charge and recurring card line for 12 months
Match each to a tool, an owner and what it does
Mark last use, and whether another tool already does the same job
List cancels with monthly savings, and the founder approves each
A person cancels them and asks site speed to remove leftover code, and the saving is logged
jobs.output: an app and subscription list with cost and use, and a signed cancel list
jobs.next: feeds 21-17 (revenue lost to slow pages) and 08-site-speed

watch.metric: monthly software cost

jobs.job: Put a dollar number on revenue lost to app scripts, including code left behind by apps already deleted: time what each script adds to load, and turn the delay into lost orders using our own conversion by load time
jobs.trigger: after 21-16, and after every app install

inputs.need: theme code and scripts on the top 5 pages
load time with and without each script
inputs.from: a free speed test tool on a copy of the theme

inputs.need: conversion by load time and device

steps: Find every script on the top 5 pages and match it to an app, live or deleted
Test page load with and without each script on a copy of the theme
From GA4, read conversion by load time band on mobile
Lost revenue = sessions times the conversion drop for the added time, times order value
Rank apps by revenue lost plus monthly fee, and send the top 5 to site speed
jobs.output: a table: app, fee, load time added, revenue lost per month, keep or remove

watch.metric: revenue lost to app load time per month

jobs.job: Each month group every bank and card line into 12 cost lines, compare them with plan, flag lines 10 percent over, and list every new recurring charge
steps: Put each line into one of 12 cost lines
Compare each line with plan and with last month
Flag lines 10 percent or more over plan
List charges that are new this month and repeat
Founder marks each flag: expected, cut, or ask
jobs.output: an overhead against plan table, and a new charges list

watch.metric: overhead against plan by line

jobs.job: Track sales and order counts by ship-to state over the last 12 months against each state's sales tax limit, and list states within 20 percent of the limit and states over it with no registration

inputs.need: each state's sales and order count limit
inputs.from: public limits typed into a sheet once, checked yearly

inputs.need: marketplace orders where the marketplace collects the tax

steps: Sum sales and order counts by state over the rolling 12 months, leaving out orders where the marketplace collects
Compare each state with its limit
List states over the limit with no registration, and states within 20 percent
Send the list to the accountant, who registers or confirms
jobs.output: a monthly state list: over, near, registered

watch.metric: states within 20 percent of their limit, and states over it with no registration

jobs.job: Show what each payment method costs per order (card, PayPal, Shop Pay, buy now pay later) next to its order value and repeat rate, and decide which to keep

inputs.need: fees and orders by payment method
PayPal and buy now pay later fee reports
checkout steps by payment method, where tracked

steps: Compute fees as a share of revenue by method
Compute order value and repeat rate by method
Estimate sales lost if a method were removed, from its share of checkouts
Founder decides, and any change is tested for 4 weeks
jobs.output: a fee table by payment method, and a keep or drop decision

watch.metric: payment fees as a share of revenue, by method

new_enablers.name: 13 week cash forecast
new_enablers.what: Starts from today's bank balance, adds expected payouts by day, and subtracts bills, payroll, supplier deposits and balances, the ad plan, loan payments and tax set aside. Marks the lowest day against the cash floor, and lets you try a change (an order, a loan, a draw) before you commit.
inputs: payout schedules per processor and marketplace
powers: the lowest cash day and the gap to the floor

new_enablers.name: Money match
new_enablers.what: Checks every dollar in and out: expected payouts against bank deposits, store sales against processor and books, and each bank and card line against a cost line and its plan. Names each gap.
powers: one sales number everyone agrees on

new_enablers.name: Sales tax watch
new_enablers.what: Sales and order counts by ship-to state over the rolling 12 months against each state's limit, with registration and filing status, so the brand registers before it owes. Other markets use the same watch with their own tax rules.
inputs: marketplace orders where the marketplace collects
